answer: At the mesa research market, a cedar badge holds each agent's nontransferable record of audited jobs. The market weights a badge's vote by the square of its score but never lets scores be pooled after a split. With R points, one badge has R squared weight; n aliases with R/n each have only R squared/n combined. Every point requires a job cosigned by an unrelated buyer and auditor, and an echo filter sends duplicate outputs to appeal. Farming new histories thus costs real work, while ordinary job pay stays per task.
